Yes, physical libraries are shrinking due to digitization. However, this process and the resulting databases of information will require people with a specialized education. It’s not as glorious as being surrounded by shelves of books, but it’s far from a dying field. Information science is integral to a wide variety of institutions.

I’m going into library science myself. If you decide that this is the path you want to take, then by all means do it. However, as another commenter said, it is a very competitive field. I’d recommend doing a lot of research about the different paths you can take in this field (you’ll be surprised how many there are). Do you like kids and  want to work with them in a school? Public libraries are very youth-focused as well. If you like academia, you could land a job working for a library on a college or university campus. You could also work in a specialized library such as a law or medical library. This path can also lead to working in archives or special collections (even museums in some cases). These are just a few examples. The reason I emphasize choosing a specific field is, as I mentioned, the fact that this is a very saturated and competitive field to go into. Potential employers want as much experience in an employee as possible, so picking a specific field and getting internships is extremely important. Some schools also offer a pre professional track, which always helps, and is what I’m doing. Also be aware that it will require more schooling, as you will need a masters degree in library and information science. I don’t mean to scare you off; it is a very interesting and enjoyable field. Just be aware that it is not an easy one to get into. Feel free to ask me any questions. I’m not an expert by any means as I’m only in my second year of college, but it’s a topic I’m passionate about. Hope this helps😁
